Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Product Designers at Stripe are strategic partners to Engineering and Product Management. Together, we define user-facing experiences, then translate that thinking into complete products that can be tested, shipped, and refined. We’re responsible for creating powerful, well-crafted, beautiful products that users love and are eager to recommend to others.

Treasury brings business banking and payments together on Stripe. We help businesses receive, store, send, and spend their money in one place — with faster access to funds, global money movement, and cards for everyday spending. Instead of stitching together banks, payment processors, and financial tools, businesses can manage their money where they already run their payments.

Our ambition is to make managing business finances feel as intuitive and thoughtfully designed as the best consumer products. That means making sophisticated capabilities accessible, bringing clarity to complex workflows, and paying close attention to the details that help people feel confident and in control of their money.

What you’ll do

As a Product Designer on the Treasury team, you’ll help rethink an essential part of running a business. Your work could help businesses access their earnings sooner, understand their cash flow, move money across currencies and borders, or manage everyday spending — all within a connected experience on Stripe.

You’ll work across new and existing products, shaping zero-to-one experiences and refining the details of what’s already in users’ hands. You’ll partner closely with Product and Engineering to define problems, explore possibilities, and bring high-quality experiences to life. This work involves substantial ambiguity and technical and regulatory complexity; your role is to make the experience feel simple without losing the rigor that financial products demand.

Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end product design process, from understanding user needs and defining problems through prototyping, detailed design, launch, and iteration.
  • Design intuitive, cohesive experiences that help businesses receive, store, send, and spend money with confidence.
  • Bring clarity to ambiguous problems, using research, exploration, and prototypes to establish direction and turn early ideas into products people can use.
  • Deliver exceptional interaction and visual design, bringing a consumer-grade standard of usability, polish, and care to complex financial tools.
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to shape the roadmap around meaningful, measurable user outcomes.
  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and other stakeholders to understand constraints and find thoughtful solutions that protect users without introducing unnecessary friction.
  • Work with user researchers, content designers, and other product designers to validate ideas and create a consistent experience across Treasury and the broader Stripe Dashboard.
  • Work closely with engineers through implementation, refining interactions and details so the shipped experience meets the intended quality bar.
  • Share work regularly in design reviews, explain your decisions clearly, and use feedback to strengthen your work.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • Have 6+ years of relevant product design experience at a technology, product-driven company.
  • Have strong visual design, interaction design, and prototyping skills, demonstrated through shipped experiences with a high bar for craft and usability.
  • Can make complex products feel simple and approachable, with thoughtful information hierarchy, clear interactions, and meticulous attention to detail.
  • Are comfortable working through substantial ambiguity: defining problems, exploring alternatives, and making progress when requirements are incomplete or evolving.
  • Can engage deeply with technical and regulatory requirements, working with cross-functional partners to translate constraints into clear, trustworthy user experiences.
  • Have worked autonomously on substantial product initiatives, partnering with Product and Engineering to shape both direction and execution.
  • Have experience working with and contributing to an established design system, balancing consistency with the needs of new experiences.
  • Have experience collaborating closely with engineers to deliver high-quality interfaces.
  • Communicate your thinking clearly through prototypes, user flows, and design rationale, and actively seek feedback.
  • Can prioritize effectively across projects at different stages, balancing speed, scope, and quality.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience shaping zero-to-one products, from early exploration through launch.
  • Experience designing financial products, particularly business accounts, money management, payments, or spending tools.
  • Experience designing consumer products, or bringing a comparable standard of simplicity and craft to complex business software.
  • Experience connecting fragmented tools or workflows into a cohesive product experience.
  • Enjoy collaborating with other designers, sharing feedback, and helping one another grow.

Company Description

About us

Solflare is a Solana self-custody wallet that puts people in control of their digital assets. Around 4 million users control $20 billion in funds through our wallet.

What started as a team of 6 in 2020 building Solana's first wallet, has grown into a team of 150 worldwide. We’re remote-first, but if you happen to stop by in Zagreb, Croatia, or Belgrade or Novi Sad, Serbia, we have an office you can work from if that’s what you prefer. 

Wherever we work, we share the same goal: a Web3 wallet for everyone, with financial freedom in their hands.

Job Description

The role

As a Backend Developer, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining the backend infrastructure of our applications, ensuring high performance, security, and scalability. You’ll work closely with the rest of the engineering team to tackle complex technical challenges and build solutions that can handle the unique demands of a crypto wallet app. 

Core responsibilities:

  • Design and implement scalable and robust backend services.
  • Develop APIs and integrate third-party services and Solana RPCs.
  • Manage databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB) and ensure data integrity and security.
  • Implement caching mechanisms using Redis for improved performance.
  • Work with PrismaJS for efficient database access and management.
  • Deploy and manage applications on cloud platforms (DigitalOcean, Google Cloud Platform).
  • Utilize BullJS for background job processing and Cron for scheduling tasks.
  • Write unit and integration tests using Jest to ensure code quality and reliability.
  • Collaborate with frontend developers and other team members to ensure seamless integration.
  • Stay updated with the latest trends and technologies in web development and blockchain.
  • Design and implement a microservices architecture for scalability and maintainability.

Qualifications

Requirements

  • Minimum of 4 years of experience in backend development with a focus on web2/web3 technologies.
  • Proficient in Node.js, Express.js, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and PrismaJS.
  • Experience with cloud services (Google Cloud Platform, DigitalOcean) and DevOps practices.
  • Experience with unit and integrations test using Jest.
  • Knowledge of event-based architecture, microservices design patterns, and ability to design scalable systems.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.

Nice to Have: 

  • Familiarity with blockchain technologies, specifically Solana, is a plus.
  • Proficiency in machine learning concepts and experience in applying them to real-world problems.
  • Experience in designing and optimizing backends to handle large volumes of data efficiently.

Additional Information

You might not like it here...

But you might love it. Working at Solflare comes with trade-offs, and we’re open about them.

Crypto moves fast, and our priorities can shift with it. We launch new features and rethink existing projects as our users’ needs evolve, in bull and bear markets alike. That means a project you expected to work on may give way to a more pressing priority. We understand this can be energizing if you can adapt and reset as you go, and frustrating if you prefer long-term predictability.

We also highly rate how people work together. Yes, individual work matters, but so does helping others succeed. We share responsibility for the outcome, and we share credit for the wins.

Our remote-first setup gives you flexibility over how you work. It also means owning your role and proactively communicating with your team, not waiting for check-ins or constant direction.

A Web3 background isn’t a must, but interest in Solflare and the industry is. Using the product, asking questions, and contributing ideas is part of every role.

You don’t have to prefer this setup. But understanding it should help you decide whether you’d enjoy working here.

 

 

Millions already use what we build. Help shape what comes next. Apply below, or check out our careers site to learn more about our culture and benefits.

The 4 biggest blockchain strengths are also its weakness

  • Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

  • Decentralization leads to too many standards

  • Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

  • Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.

Blockchains are optimized for writes, not reads.

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

  • Fragmented standards

  • Exponential complexity

  • No accountability for interpretation

  • Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

Allium is building the System of Record for Onchain Finance

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

  • Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

  • Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

  • Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

  • Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.

Finance is moving onchain

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability.

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Who We Serve

Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation:

1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators.

2. Engineers and Product Teams They need low latency, production ready infrastructure. They use Allium to power wallets, trading systems, payment rails, staking infrastructure, and real time applications that cannot break.

3. Strategy, Research, and Executive Teams They need clarity and insight. They use Allium to understand ecosystem economics, market structure, user behavior, competitive dynamics, and where capital is flowing onchain.

And of course...agents 🦞. Our customers and users include Visa, Stripe, G-SIB Banks, Big 4 Accounting firms, BCG, Coinbase, Phantom, Uniswap and cited by the Federal Reserve.

About the role

We're hiring a Security Engineer to build and operate the controls that protect Allium's infrastructure, applications, employee systems, and use of AI. You'll work closely with Engineering and the person leading our security program to investigate threats, implement practical fixes, and automate security work.

As AI agents gain access to code, data, and tools, security needs to cover both human and machine activity. You'll help secure how agents operate while strengthening our defenses against automated attacks, credential theft, and compromised software dependencies. This is a hands-on engineering role: you'll write code, test controls, investigate real signals, and take findings through remediation.

What you'll do

  • Secure cloud infrastructure and access. Implement least privilege, phishing-resistant authentication, short-lived credentials, controlled privileged access, and reliable provisioning and deprovisioning. Improve cloud configuration, managed credential storage, and network protections with service owners. Improve secrets scanning and prevent credentials from entering source control.

  • Secure AI agents and developer tools. Help implement permissions, execution isolation, network restrictions, and audit trails for coding assistants, agents, and tool integrations, including MCP. Test how untrusted content could trigger prompt injection, tool misuse, or unintended data access, and build safeguards at the point where actions execute.

  • Build detection and response. Correlate identity, cloud, workload, and CI/CD telemetry to detect credential theft, unusual access, unauthorized agent actions, suspicious software changes, and data exfiltration. Investigate attacks across systems, reduce alert noise, and test response procedures with system owners, including session revocation, exposed-credential rotation, and removal of unauthorized access.

  • Reduce software supply-chain risk. Assess dependencies, CI/CD workflows, third-party integrations, and developer environments. Partner with engineers to validate findings, protect build and deployment credentials, and remediate vulnerabilities.

  • Move quickly on relevant threats. Maintain visibility into internet-facing services, including developer tools and management interfaces. Evaluate new vulnerabilities and active exploitation against our actual exposure. Help patch, isolate, revoke credentials, or apply compensating controls with service owners, then verify that the response worked.

  • Automate and document. Use code and APIs to improve access reviews, configuration checks, evidence collection, and remediation tracking. Use AI thoughtfully for security work, validating its output and protecting sensitive data.

  • Support employee security and enterprise assurance. Deploy, validate, and maintain endpoint protections and device security baselines, including prevention settings, tamper protection, encryption, and timely updates. Work with the owner of employee IT on identity and SaaS controls. Provide clear technical evidence for audits and customer reviews, and maintain useful runbooks.

The Capacity & Efficiency Engineering team builds the software that manages, governs, and reduces Robinhood's AWS cloud spend across compute, databases, and storage, operating at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, data engineering, and FinOps. We own the full lifecycle of cloud cost, from attribution and forecasting to automation that rightsizes infrastructure at fleet scale and keeps a bursty, latency-sensitive trading platform both reliable and cost-effective. Our work carries CEO-level visibility, has already driven millions of dollars in annualized savings, and is delivered in close partnership with Infrastructure, Finance, and product engineering teams across Robinhood.

As a Senior Software Engineer on the team, you will own capacity and efficiency for Robinhood's storage and database fleet, from Aurora clusters to S3 and the caches and volumes in between. You will build the systems that size this fleet to demand: Aurora reader counts and writer sizes set from market hours, declared events, and live load instead of fixed schedules; databases, caches, and volumes rightsized to what they actually use; and S3 data kept in the right storage class, with lifecycle rules that keep growth in check. You will take each from recommendations the Storage team validates to automation that safely applies its own changes in production. This is a 0-to-1 build with measurable impact on reliability at market peaks and on the AWS bill.

This role is based in our Bellevue, WA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

  • Build forecast-driven capacity planning for the storage and database fleet, turning traffic history, load tests, and known events (market open, earnings, IPOs, promotions) into plans that scale up ahead and back down after, with an expiry on every temporary capacity hold
  • Design and build a capacity planner for Aurora that sets reader counts and writer instance sizes from demand and load signals (IOPS, CPU, connections, replica lag), replacing fixed scaling schedules
  • Rightsize databases, caches, and block storage (RDS, ElastiCache, DynamoDB, EBS) on instance size, provisioned IOPS and throughput, and idle capacity, and keep them right-sized as load changes
  • Own S3 efficiency at scale: storage class and Intelligent-Tiering strategy, lifecycle and retention policies, noncurrent versions and incomplete uploads, and request costs, using Storage Lens and inventory data
  • Take every recommendation to closed-loop automation with guardrails, progressive rollout, and rollback, in partnership with the Storage infrastructure team, handling constraints such as AWS capacity shortages, fallback instance types, and connection pooling
  • Measure outcomes in cost and reliability (savings against baseline, forecast error, utilization, capacity left behind after events) and share our forecasts with the pod rightsizing system so compute and storage scale together

  • Strong Python or Go engineering, with experience building automation that safely modifies production infrastructure (guardrails, progressive rollout, and rollback built in), not just systems that observe and report

Protective Intelligence is zerohash’s security function responsible for the safety of our people.. This is a hands-on, individually accountable role: you’ll own daily operations and case decisions directly, from monitoring and triage through vendor management and executive travel security planning.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and remediate digital risk alerts, online impersonation, and brand abuse.
  • Assess and manage threat cases for executives and their families with appropriate sensitivity and rigor.
  • Determine executive protection coverage and travel-related security risks, including international travel.
  • Conduct risk assessments for residential physical security, company office locations, and hosted events or public appearances.
  • Build law enforcement relationships and coordinate with Legal prior to engagement.
  • Manage digital risk monitoring vendors, program budget, and documentation.
  • Deliver security awareness briefings to enrolled executives and report activity to leadership.

Requirements

  • Background in corporate security, executive protection, protective intelligence, or law enforcement/federal investigative experience
  • Familiarity with OSINT research and digital-risk monitoring tools is a plus, not required on day one
  • Comfortable being the single point of accountability
  • Sound judgment with sensitive personal information about executives and their families, and the discretion that comes with it
  • Able to work directly and credibly with senior leaders and their support staff without a layer of management in between
  • Available for time-sensitive escalations outside standard hours as the primary after-hours escalation contact, with backup coverage from Risk leadership

  • Maternity & Paternity leave (after 6 months)
  • WeWork All Access Membership
  • WFH Yearly Stipend
  • L&D Yearly Stipend (after 6 months)

About zerohash

zerohash is the leading crypto and stablecoin infrastructure platform and the operating system for digital money, powering the next generation of financial services. Founded in 2017, zerohash enables banks, brokerages, fintechs, and payment companies to offer crypto trading, stablecoin payments, and tokenized assets without having to build or manage complex blockchain infrastructure on their own.

The zerohash platform supports three core pillars: Trade, Transact, and Tokenize. Through a single integration, customers can launch regulated crypto buy, sell, and custody services; enable 24/7 stablecoin-based funding, payouts, and settlement; and issue and manage tokenized assets with built-in compliance, risk controls, and reporting. By abstracting away technical, regulatory, and operational complexity, zerohash allows partners to treat digital assets as just another financial primitive: fast, programmable, and global.

zerohash is trusted by some of the world’s most recognized financial and consumer brands, including Interactive Brokers, Morgan Stanley, Stripe, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock, DraftKings, Gusto, Worldpay, Kalshi, One Pay, among others. Today, zerohash infrastructure supports millions of end users across brokerage, wealth, payments, and marketplace platforms globally.

The company is deeply regulated and compliance-first, operating across the U.S. and internationally with licenses and approvals that allow partners to enter crypto and stablecoins with confidence. zerohash has become a trusted partner for enterprises seeking to modernize financial products while meeting the highest standards for security, risk management, and regulatory oversight.

To date, zerohash has raised over $280 million in funding from a mix of leading venture firms and strategic investors, including Morgan Stanley, Interactive Brokers, SoFi, Point72 Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and more.

zerohash has been featured in top-tier media outlets such as Bloomberg, CNBC, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Reuters, Forbes, and CoinDesk, and its leadership team regularly contributes to global conversations on the future of payments, investing, and financial infrastructure.

At zerohash, we're building the infrastructure that makes digital money work securely, compliantly, and at global scale.

The zerohash Culture

All zerohash employees are guided by the following characteristics and core principles:

  • Independence/Ownership - An ability to work autonomously. Join zerohash, pitch ideas, and shape the work you do.
  • Passion - We are innovating quickly and challenging the status quo. We want you to think big, be creative and ​make a difference every day.
  • Collaborative - A good attitude and respect for others. We’re teammates, not co-workers. Everything we do is a shared success and equally a shared failure - we talk in terms of “we” not “me”.
  • Initiative - An ability and passion for learning and asking questions. We will champion you, challenge you and push you to achieve your best - and we expect you to do the same.
  • Empathy - An ability to listen, respect, and understand your co-workers, customers, and everyone you interact with no matter how different they are to you.
  • Adaptability - An ability to respond quickly. We are in a fast-paced industry and so we expect you to be creative when solving a new problem and comfortable under pressure.
  • Transparency - We believe that transparency is critical to empowering everyone to make the best decisions, both the company to its people and vice versa.
  • Integrity - Integrity creates trust. As both an organization collectively and as individuals, it is our most valuable asset.

The R&D team at Chainalysis is inspired by solving the hardest technical challenges and building products that establish trust in cryptocurrencies. We're a global organization that thrives on challenging work and doing it alongside exceptionally talented teammates. Our industry evolves rapidly, and our mission is to build a flexible, AI-driven platform that automates entity resolution, optimizes data labeling pipelines, and creates predictive models that identify illicit patterns before they escalate.

Chainalysis data has helped solve some of the world’s highest-profile criminal and national-security cases and made it safer for people everywhere to access crypto. The Global Intelligence Team produces the attribution at the heart of that data — connecting on-chain activity to the real-world entities behind it, across the global crypto ecosystem. It’s the intelligence data moat beneath every Chainalysis product, and what investigators, sanctions authorities, and national-security agencies rely on to follow the money and disrupt threats.

Few domains demand more sustained depth than Russia and the broader Eurasian sanctions-evasion ecosystem. Since 2022, sweeping sanctions on Russian financial institutions, oligarchs, and the defense-industrial base have pushed a growing share of Russian value flows into cryptocurrency — from no-KYC exchanges and OTC desks operating across the former Soviet bloc, to sanctions-evasion networks exploiting stablecoins and cross-border payment channels, crypto-denominated procurement of restricted goods, and the financial infrastructure supporting Russian cyber and ransomware operations. Understanding how Russian actors adapt to sanctions pressure on-chain is one of the most consequential problems in crypto intelligence today.

As our Russia & Eurasia-focused intelligence analyst — the team’s subject-matter expert on Russian and Eurasian crypto threats — you’ll own that problem end to end. This is a depth role: while our analysts cover the breadth of the crypto-services ecosystem, you’ll go deep on a single, high-stakes domain — becoming the person, inside Chainalysis and increasingly across the industry, who understands how Russian and Eurasian actors use crypto to evade sanctions and can prove it on-chain. You’ll own the attribution for Russia’s crypto footprint, map how these networks operate and adapt under pressure, turn that into finished intelligence customers act on, and be the expert voice representing Chainalysis on Russian crypto threats.

Who you’ll work with

You’ll join a fast-moving, globally distributed team — analysts, threat-domain SMEs, data scientists, and engineers — collaborating across time zones, async and in real time. We move fast, hold each other to a high bar, and back each other up across regions. As the Russia & Eurasia SME, you’ll be the single point of depth for the domain and a force multiplier for everyone working adjacent to it.

In this role, you’ll:

  • Own Russia & Eurasia attribution end to end — the threat-actor entities, their definitions, and the accounts, addresses, and infrastructure they operate: Russian and CIS no-KYC exchanges, OTC networks, and instant swap services, sanctions-evasion infrastructure (stablecoin corridors, cross-border payment channels, nested services), Russian-linked ransomware and cybercrime ecosystem financial flows, procurement networks for restricted and dual-use goods, and the broader financial infrastructure enabling Russian value movement outside the traditional financial system.

  • Lead the attribution response to Russia-related sanctions events — when OFAC or allied authorities designate Russian entities, actors, or infrastructure, drive the rapid, high-visibility on-chain attribution that turns those designations into coverage in our data, often against the clock.

  • Map the networks on-chain — trace how Russian and Eurasian actors raise, move, launder, and cash out value through regional exchanges, no-KYC swaps, OTC desks, stablecoin corridors, mixers, and off-ramps across the former Soviet bloc and beyond, and keep that picture current as they adapt to pressure.

  • Produce finished intelligence — advisory notes, customer and partner briefings, and contributions to flagship publications (the Crypto Crime Report and beyond) that make the Russia & Eurasia crypto threat legible and actionable.

  • Be the named external expert — represent Chainalysis on Russia & Eurasia crypto threats at conferences, on panels, with the press, and in briefings to public- and private-sector partners.

  • Help set the Russia & Eurasia collection agenda — surface what data we need on Russian and Eurasian networks and feed those requirements into our collection process and priority intelligence requirements; you direct collection for the domain, but it runs through the team’s apparatus and prioritization, not you alone.

  • Translate typologies into detection — turn what you learn about Russian methods and sanctions-evasion typologies into guidance that our products and our customers can operationalize.

  • Build with AI — design and tune the automation that scales your analysis and the team’s, and handle the hard cases automation can’t.

  • Level up the team — raise the bar on Russia & Eurasia and sanctions-evasion tradecraft broadly, and partner closely with analysts, other SMEs, data science, and engineering.

We’re looking for candidates who have:

  • Deep, demonstrable Russia & Eurasia expertise — real command of the Russian sanctions landscape, Russian financial infrastructure and how it has adapted to sanctions pressure, the CIS/former Soviet bloc crypto ecosystem, and/or Russian illicit-finance and procurement networks. This is the core of the role, and we’ll expect you to show it.

  • On-chain tracing ability against Russian targets — direct experience following Russian crypto activity on-chain (Russian exchanges, sanctions evasion, ransomware financial flows), or deep Russia threat-finance expertise paired with proven blockchain-tracing skill you can bring to bear here from day one.

  • A national-security or threat-finance background — intelligence, sanctions, counter-threat-finance, or investigations, from the IC, Treasury/OFAC, law enforcement, the military, a think tank or research institution, or private-sector CTF/sanctions work.

  • Regional fluency — a strong grasp of Russian and Eurasian geopolitics, the sanctions landscape, and regional financial flows. Russian language ability is a significant plus.

  • Elite potential and a proven track record — exceptional aptitude, judgment, and work ethic; you’ve led hard problems end to end and you raise everyone around you.

  • Excellent writing and communication — this is an outward-facing expert role; your intelligence has to land with analysts, customers, and senior audiences alike.

  • AI-forward instincts — you build automation to scale your work and others’, not just use it.

  • Comfort working with data; blockchain forensics experience strongly preferred.

  • 5+ years of relevant analytic, intelligence, or threat-finance experience for a Senior hire; 8+ years and recognized domain authority for a Staff hire.

You might also have:

  • Russian language ability.

  • Direct experience with OFAC, EU, or OFSI sanctions, sanctions-evasion investigations, or the designation process.

  • A record of published research or public speaking on Russia, sanctions evasion, or crypto threat finance.

  • Familiarity with Russian and CIS exchange infrastructure, stablecoin-based sanctions evasion, ransomware financial flows, or dual-use procurement networks.

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here. 

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

Own Your Intelligence

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators, including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.

Role Impact

Build the data behind Prime Intellect’s next generation of open models. You’ll find valuable sources, turn them into training-ready corpora, and work with researchers to test what actually improves the model. Your work will shape both broad pre-training and the data used to develop reasoning, coding, and long-context capabilities.

Responsibilities

  • Find, evaluate, and collect valuable training data from web, code, and technical sources.

  • Build scalable pipelines that turn raw data into training-ready corpora through extraction, cleaning, deduplication, and filtering.

  • Develop checks for data quality, coverage, and contamination, and use them to improve collection and processing.

  • Work with researchers on data mixtures and sampling strategies for pre-training and midtraining.

  • Prepare and evaluate data for long-context learning, reasoning, and coding, testing synthetic data where it proves useful.

  • Run controlled data experiments and use model evaluations to decide which sources, mixtures, and processing choices are worth scaling.

  • Make large-scale data processing efficient, reproducible, and recoverable, with clear source provenance and dataset versioning.

Requirements

  • Strong programming skills in Python and a record of building reliable data-processing or distributed systems.

  • Experience working with large datasets and managing the practical tradeoffs of storage, compute, throughput, and reproducibility.

  • Ability to diagnose data-quality issues and translate research goals into measurable checks and experiments.

  • Comfort owning an evolving technical problem end to end and working closely with researchers to test assumptions and improve the system.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Web crawling, document extraction, code-data collection, or large-scale corpus curation.

  • Deduplication, text classification, quality scoring, synthetic data, or training-data contamination analysis.

  • Data-mixture experiments, curriculum learning, or measuring how dataset changes affect model performance.

Nice to have

  • Experience preparing datasets for language-model pre-training, continued pre-training, or midtraining.

  • Work with distributed processing frameworks such as Spark, Ray, or comparable systems.

  • Experience with multilingual, mathematical, scientific, or repository-level code data.

  • Familiarity with tokenization, training data loaders, and the needs of large model-training runs.
